questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Draw a supported historical inference from evidence of early mark-making.
questions.prompt: Archaeologists reported pieces of red ochre with engraved designs from Middle Stone Age layers at Blombos Cave in South Africa. Which statement can a museum label support using this evidence?
questions.answer: People made deliberate designs on pieces of ochre during the Middle Stone Age.
questions.explanation: The designs and their excavation context provide evidence of early mark-making. The objects alone cannot establish the intended meaning or the first place people made art.
options: The designs record the names of the people who made them.
People made deliberate designs on pieces of ochre during the Middle Stone Age.
The same designs were used throughout Africa at that time.
The cave is the first place where people ever made art.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Explain the limits of a claim about the origin of art based on an excavated object.
questions.prompt: A school exhibition label calls the Blombos Cave engravings “the first art anyone ever made.” Rewrite that claim as a defensible sentence and give one reason the stronger claim goes beyond the find.
questions.answer: The engraved ochre from Blombos Cave provides evidence of early deliberate design. Older examples may have perished or may still be undiscovered.
questions.explanation: Excavation provides evidence of what survives in a particular context. It cannot settle where or when every form of art began.

markingGuide.description: Identifies engraved ochre from Blombos Cave as evidence.
Makes a limited claim about early design.
Explains how survival, discovery or the limited context prevents establishing a universal first.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Explain how artistic decisions convey a feeling.
questions.prompt: Two pupils draw the same empty classroom. One uses widely spaced desks and long shadows to suggest loneliness. Explain how the pupil’s choices turn a familiar place into an expression of a feeling.
questions.answer: The gaps make the room look empty and the long shadows can make it feel still or isolated. The pupil arranges visible features to communicate a feeling about the place.
questions.explanation: An artwork can communicate a viewpoint through deliberate decisions about what to show and how to show it.

markingGuide.description: Identifies at least one deliberate visual choice.
Connects the choice to a plausible feeling.
Explains how this makes the drawing an expression of the pupil’s viewpoint.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Explain how moving water can carry and deposit fine clay particles.
questions.prompt: Water carries tiny particles away from weathered ground and into a sheltered basin. A fine layer gradually builds on the bottom. Explain how the particles travelled and why they could collect in that basin.
questions.answer: Flowing water carried the fine particles in suspension. Where water movement was weak enough for long enough, particles could settle and gradually form a layer.
questions.explanation: Clay deposits can form when transported fine material accumulates. The example describes deposition, one route by which clay-rich layers form.

markingGuide.description: Explains settling where the water becomes sufficiently quiet.
Connects repeated settling to accumulation of the layer.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Recognise plasticity as a useful property of moist modelling clay.
questions.prompt: At an art table, a material can be pressed into a shallow cup while moist and keeps the new shape when the pressure is removed. Which property is the pupil making use of?
questions.explanation: Plasticity allows a suitably moist clay body to deform under pressure and retain the changed shape.

questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts
questions.learningObjective: Select a preparation step for clay with uneven moisture.
questions.prompt: A teacher provides modelling clay with some firm patches and some soft patches. Which action best prepares the clay for a small hand-modelled form?
questions.answer: Work it until the moisture and consistency are reasonably even.
questions.explanation: An even consistency lets the clay respond more predictably when pressed or rolled.
options: Dust only the outside with dry powder and keep the patches inside.
Shape the piece immediately with all the soft clay on one side.
Work it until the moisture and consistency are reasonably even.
Expose only the firm patches to warm moving air.
